name: Akiflow
tagline: Command-center planner that merges tasks, calendar, and time blocking

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Pro Monthly listed at $34/month and annual at $19/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1 user; tasks, calendars, integrations, and time blocking; no numeric task/calendar cap published.
tiers.notes: Annual price is a promoted 44% discount.

tiers.name: Teams
tiers.limits: Custom seats, onboarding, and team controls.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-44% advertised); 7-day trial; Teams custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: The $19 annual equivalent is promotional; renewal terms beyond the displayed offer are not stated publicly.

verdictSummary: The planner UI can be built, but bringing every task source into one reliable, two-way calendar workflow means OAuth, APIs, sync conflicts, and maintenance.
coreLoopDIY: Ingest tasks from selected tools, show an inbox, drag into a calendar, create time blocks, and push updates back.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay to stop context-switching between task apps and calendars.

priorArt.name: Super Productivity
priorArt.desc: Open-source personal productivity app that covers portions of time blocking and task plann

alternatives.name: FlowSavvy Free
alternatives.desc: It auto-plans unlimited tasks for the next two weeks; priorities and dependencies are how the paid plan gets you.

facts.install: Create a hosted account in the web app or install the iOS or Android app
facts.engines: A deterministic scheduling algorithm; FlowSavvy explicitly says it does not use machine learning to build schedules
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, events, and settings live in FlowSavvy's cloud database and synchronize with connected Google, Outlook, or iCloud calendars; the service currently provides no general calendar import or export
facts.gapVsPaid: FlowSavvy auto-schedules tasks but lacks Akiflow’s universal inbox, broad task-source integrations, command bar, and free priority and dependency controls.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires an internet connection; calendar synchronization requires OAuth or app-specific credentials

alternatives.name: Super Productivity
alternatives.desc: A local task planner with timeboxes, focus mode and its own stopwatch; less glossy, less interested in your wallet.

facts.install: Use the browser/PWA or install a packaged desktop or mobile build
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, time records, and settings are local-first in browser or app storage; optional synchronization and backups use the user's chosen WebDAV or Dropbox account
facts.gapVsPaid: Super Productivity timeboxes local tasks well but does not pull a broad set of external task systems into one inbox or automatically place them on the calendar like Akiflow.

alternatives.name: Trevor AI Free
alternatives.desc: One calendar gets task-to-time-block planning and some AI suggestions; multiple calendars and deeper automation cost extra.

facts.install: Create a hosted web account and connect one supported calendar; the web app can be installed to a home screen
facts.engines: A private per-user deep-learning scheduling model; some language features use OpenAI, according to Trevor's documentation
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, calendar events, and scheduling state are processed and stored in Trevor's hosted infrastructure, with connected calendar data synchronized through provider APIs
facts.gapVsPaid: Trevor’s free plan supports one calendar and a web-only planner, without Akiflow’s native command center, universal inbox, and integration breadth.
facts.setupBlocker: No native desktop or mobile app; calendar integrations require OAuth, and the free tier is limited to one calendar account

rejectedAlternatives.name: Amplenote Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan has an internal calendar, but syncing the external calendar you already use requires Pro.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ellie Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free task list is pleasant; timebox mode and calendar integrations are both Pro.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Routine Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan stops before time blocking and time boxing; the feature this comparison is about starts paid.

notes: Expensive enough to make DIY tempting; integration upkeep keeps it kinda.
prompt:
Build me a daily planner with time blocking to replace Akiflow. Requirements:

- Local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3; the day/week grid is
  FullCalendar with vanilla JS, no build step.
- A capture inbox: one text box, Enter saves a task; tasks have title,
  minutes estimate (default 30), and a done flag.
- Drag a task from the inbox sidebar onto the grid to create a time block;
  drag to move or resize; block and task stay linked, completing one
  completes the other.
- My real calendar shows behind the blocks as a read-only overlay of ICS
  feed URLs from .env; Google Calendar's secret ICS address works and needs
  no OAuth.
- Keyboard-first: n for new task, t for today, arrows move selection, Enter
  schedules the selected task into the next free slot.
- Morning rollover: unfinished blocks from yesterday return to the inbox
  with a reschedule counter, so chronically avoided tasks are visible.
- SQLite storage, localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: two-way Google/Outlook sync and pulling tasks in from other
  apps. Read-only overlay only; OAuth plus sync-conflict handling is exactly
  the maintenance that makes Akiflow worth paying for.
- README: how to find a calendar's secret ICS URL.
